http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: CR 113.3 partitions abilities into exactly these four kinds; a disjoint union states that partition rather than merely listing subclasses.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: A rules description carried by a card design or game object, defining tasks its controller may or must perform.
Win by dealing damage quickly with efficient threats.
A recognised deck description that satisfies a strategy and is typically realised by a characteristic card set.
Forest, Island, Mountain, Plains, Swamp (CR 305.6).

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Oracle names are unique across the card pool; declaring the key lets a reasoner merge duplicate design nodes from different importers.

v1.x conflated the card design, the physical printing, and the in-game object under one Card class, which made it impossible to state that two printings share oracle text or that a token has no design.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value:
The abstract card as a piece of rules text — "Lightning
        Bolt" as designed, independent of any printing or any game. This is
        what Scryfall's oracle entry denotes.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: DUL Information Realization pattern: the printing realizes the design.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: A concrete printing of a card design in a given set, with its own collector number, artwork and frame.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Separates classification concepts from the objects they classify; permitted class/individual punning alone does not provide a semantic bridge between those levels.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value:
A type concept that *classifies* card designs and game
        objects. Modelled as a Concept, not as a class, because types change
        during a game (an animated land) — a subsumption axiom cannot be
        retracted, a classification can.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: A combo prescribes tasks; dul:Plan is the DOLCE category for descriptions that define tasks.
A one-card 'combo' is just a card; the qualified min-2 cardinality is the definitional constraint and was previously only a SHACL shape.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value:
A plan whose execution over two or more card designs
        produces a characteristic outcome. Modelling a combo as a Plan rather
        than a bag of cards is what lets setup requirements, ordering, and the
        produced outcome be stated.
Win by assembling a specific card interaction.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Makes 'which rule licenses this modelling choice?' a graph query rather than a comment.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: A numbered section of the Magic Comprehensive Rules, treated as the normative description that grounds a term.
Win by answering threats and accruing card advantage.
Shared between creatures and kindreds (CR 205.3m).
A normative description constraining which card designs are legal and how a game is set up.
An event with at least one player as its agent: casting, activating, attacking, blocking, passing priority.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Triggered abilities are defined over events; without a first-class Event class the trigger condition has nothing to quantify over.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: An occurrence the rules can react to: entering the battlefield, dying, dealing damage, a spell being cast.

An object existing in a game: a permanent on the
        battlefield, a card in a zone, a spell on the stack, a token, or a
        copy. Distinct from its design — a game object may have no design
        (a token) or a design it does not currently match (a face-down
        creature, a copy effect).
A quality inhering in a game object or design: power, toughness, mana value, loyalty, colour.
A role a game object or player plays within a situation: attacker, blocker, target, controller, owner, commander.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Role/Situation is the DOLCE pattern that lets the same creature be an attacker in one combat and a blocker in the next without contradictory assertions.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value:
A state of affairs in a game that roles are relative to —
        a combat, a priority window, a resolution. Role assignments
        (attacker, blocker, target) hold *in* a situation, never absolutely.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: No induced assertion may exist without the run that produced it — provenance is a modelling constraint, not a convention.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: A relation proposed by trace mining rather than curation.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Reification rather than a direct mtg:synergisesWith edge keeps the curated symmetric relation clean and lets conflicting evidence coexist.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: Reified n-ary synergy claim between two or more designs, carrying its evidence.
A named ability concept (CR 702) that classifies card designs and abilities.
A named game action defined by CR 701 (attach, exile, scry, mill, ...) that classifies game actions.
A keyword that can exist as a counter on a permanent, granting that keyword (CR 122.1b).
Win through individually powerful cards and attrition.
A concept classifying the situations a combo produces: infinite mana, arbitrarily large damage, instant win.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Defined class: being a permanent just is being on the battlefield, so it should be inferred rather than asserted.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: A game object on the battlefield.
The batch of games an induced assertion was derived from.
Shared between instants and sorceries (CR 205.3k).
A macro-level plan: aggro, midrange, control, combo, tempo, stax.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: v1.x had no subtype machinery at all, so Vehicle, Equipment, Aura, Saga and every creature type were simply unrepresentable.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: A subtype concept classifying card designs and game objects, correlated to a card type (CR 205.3c).
Basic, Legendary, Ongoing, Snow, World (CR 205.4a). Printed before the card types.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: The max-0 restriction is the formal statement of 'a token is not a card', which v1.x could only say in a comment.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: A game object with no card design behind it.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: v1.x typed power as xsd:string precisely because characteristic-defining values are not integers; the DOLCE quality/region split expresses that properly instead of degrading the datatype.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value:
The value a quality takes. Separating quality from region
        is what lets power be `*` or `X` — a region that is not a number —
        without breaking the datatype range.
A place where game objects can exist (CR 400).

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Disruption works piecewise; this chain derives combo-level answers from card-level ones instead of requiring them to be enumerated.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: Fraction of the Scryfall pool whose oracle text matches this mechanic. Measured, hence induced.

Not functional and not temporally absolute: control changes.
        Durable statements about control are made through a
        mtg:ControllerRole classification inside a mtg:GameSituation.
Asymmetric: that A answers B does not make B answer A.
CR section number that grounds this term, e.g. "702.9".
Identifier of the competency question this axiom was introduced to answer.

One of "curated" (hand-authored or derived from the
        Comprehensive Rules / Scryfall oracle data), "induced" (mined from
        self-play traces), or "proposed" (agent-generated, awaiting human
        review). Consumers that require deterministic ground truth filter to
        "curated".
Links a modelled term to the CR section that licenses it.
Functional: a quality has one value at a time. Layer-system recomputation replaces the region, it does not add one.
Game ⊐ Turn ⊐ Phase ⊐ Step ⊐ GameEvent.
Engine coverage: implemented | partial | planned | not_planned.
Functional: CR 400.5 — an object exists in exactly one zone.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Property chain replaces the boolean is_attacking flag of v1.x with a queryable, situation-relative relation.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: Symbolic cost, e.g. {2}{W}{U}. The numeric mana value is a quality with its own region.
Present only when the region is numerically determinate.
Transitive ordering of steps, phases and turns. Acyclicity is checked with SHACL; OWL 2 DL forbids asymmetry/irreflexivity axioms on transitive properties.
Why this axiom exists. Append-only; never rewritten in place.
Lexical value of a quality region — "3", "*", "1+*", "X".
Anchors a role assignment to the situation it holds in.
Top-level CR section 1-9 (Game Concepts ... Casual Variants).
Functional identifier: the CardPrinting datatype key identifies a printing by its Scryfall UUID.
Transitive: 205.3m is a sub-rule of 205.3, which is a sub-rule of 205.1.
Number of games supporting the claim. Used with refutationCount to compute confidence.
Symmetric and irreflexive. Curated synergies only — learned ones are reified as mtg:InducedSynergy.

http://purl.org/dc/terms/description.value:
An OWL 2 DL ontology of Magic: The Gathering cards,
        game mechanics, turn structure, strategic knowledge, and agent
        decision-making, aligned to DOLCE-UltraLite. Separates curated schema
        from induced (self-play-learned) evidence with PROV-O provenance.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: Designed for OWL 2 DL. Logical qualification and dependency-profile results are reported separately.

http://purl.org/dc/terms/source.value: Magic: The Gathering Comprehensive Rules, effective September 25, 2026

http://purl.org/dc/terms/title.value: MTG type system and keyword vocabulary, derived from the rules

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: Generated. See scripts/build_ontology_from_cr.py.
A software agent occupying a seat.
A distribution over hidden game state — the opponent's hand and library order.
One action selection at one priority window, with its full objective decomposition retained.
G(pi) for one candidate action: control cost plus risk.
A plan mapping belief states to action distributions.

http://purl.org/mtg/ontology#rationale.value: Anchoring preferences to plant state rather than observations is what rules out transducer wireheading; recording it as a first-class parameter makes the agent's goal specification inspectable.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: V(eta) = -ln p(eta) over latent game state. The sole encoding of goals.
Diagnostic only — deliberately not a term in the objective.
KL divergence of the controlled path against the passive prior.
Bounded-rationality parameter. beta -> infinity recovers the deterministic Bellman minimiser.
Expected terminal preference potential under the controlled path.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#lab.value: as well as any variants of those keywords

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#pref.value: as well as any variants of those keywords

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.value: Endurant / perdurant / quality / region are mutually exclusive in DOLCE.
